paper.title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control

signatures.object: Robot policy as a language-model-generated Python program (LMP) over perception and control APIs
signatures.information: instruction as a comment; hints (API imports) and few-shot instruction-code examples; object detectors (MDETR, ViLD) and control primitive APIs (pick-place, set_velocity, trajectory following)
signatures.operation: Codex generates code; static safety check; exec with globals=APIs; return value read from locals
signatures.output: executed program (feedback loops, waypoints, calls to primitives)
signatures.conditions: factorized perception and control; APIs with meaningful names; instructions feasible
signatures.feedback: none to the generator; the program itself may contain perception-conditioned loops
signatures.persistence: session history of instructions/responses lets later instructions refer back ('undo')
signatures.failure_boundary: no a priori correctness check, API scope, long or different-abstraction commands

signatures.information: AST of generated code; prompt for a function-writing LMP
signatures.operation: find undefined functions in generated code and recursively ask a function-generation LMP to define them, depth-first
signatures.conditions: meaningful verbose names; large enough Codex model
signatures.persistence: functions accumulate in the session scope
signatures.failure_boundary: gain only for davinci-class models, not cushman

retention_trace.reason: no candidate change is selected or persisted across tasks; generated functions persist only inside a session
